purpose: Screenshots of other products, used as the outside comparison for design review of the Clipping Factory studio.

roles.reference: A real application window captured at a native viewport size. These are the only files a comparative judge is scored against.
roles.aspiration: Vendor marketing art: cropped single surfaces, 720 to 1400 px wide, not a whole app window at a native size. Kept for looking at, never scored against.

note: Files marked role "reference" were captured from the running application on this machine, at the same CSS pixel sizes and device scale factor as the studio's own shots, so both sides of a comparison are the same kind of image. Files marked role "aspiration" are third-party marketing assets kept for internal design reference; each was published by its vendor. Do not redistribute either kind as part of the product.

files.captured_on: Mac mini (Apple M1, macOS 26.0.1), remote over ssh
files.method: Launched the installed app with --remote-debugging-port and captured its own Chromium renderer at a 1280x800 CSS viewport, device scale factor 1, through reference/capture-t3-window.mjs. This is the app's window content, not the vendor site and not a window screenshot with macOS chrome.
files.shows: The app's new-thread screen: sidebar with search and thread groups, breadcrumb header, the empty workspace headline, the composer with its model, reasoning, access and machine selectors, and the project panel on the right.
files.note: The sidebar shows the capture machine's own project and device names. Nothing was edited.

files.captured_on: Mac mini (Apple M1, macOS 26.0.1), remote over ssh
files.method: Same capture as t3-code-window@1280.png at a 1440x900 CSS viewport.
files.shows: The same screen at the wider viewport, where the composer stays a fixed measure and the extra width lands as margin.
files.note: The sidebar shows the capture machine's own project and device names. Nothing was edited.

files.shows: Desktop app: thread list, message timeline, composer and the right-hand inspector.
files.note: Superseded by t3-code-window@1280.png and t3-code-window@1440.png, which are the same app at native size. This one is a website asset, resized to 1400 px wide, and is not scored against.
